headline: A markets commentary account says just 42 AI stocks have produced two-thirds of the S&P 500's gains since the start of 2024.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the figures are one commentary account's own calculation on a basket of 42 stocks that is not listed, relayed by Moneycontrol.
importance_line: What changed is a striking measure of how few companies are driving the US stock market, which matters first to savers and pension holders in US share funds, then to investors who rely on the wider market, then to the AI companies at the centre, and the doubt is that the figures are an unaudited social-media calculation with no list of the stocks or method.
summary: Moneycontrol reports, citing a post by The Kobeissi Letter, a financial-markets commentary platform, that 42 AI stocks account for 67% of the S&P 500's price gains since the start of 2024, or 22 of its 33 percentage points, against 11 from the other 458 stocks. The Letter adds that the same 42 stocks account for 58% of the index's earnings growth and 81% of its growth in capital spending and research, and that only 29% of stocks have beaten the index over three years, close to the roughly 25% low of the 2000 dot-com bubble.
notes: Read in full. Moneycontrol is relaying a post on X by The Kobeissi Letter (11 Oct 2026); credit names both. The list of 42 stocks and the method are not given.
